title: The Old Way vs. The Quantum Way
style_suffix: Cinematic TV commercial, photorealistic, natural lip sync, 35mm lens, shallow depth of field, punchy contrast grade, subtle film grain. No text, no letters, no logos, no signs anywhere; any screens show only soft abstract shapes. Sound: clear natural dialogue and light room ambience.

shots.prompt: Photorealistic portrait of a cheerful, slightly smug middle-aged man called Busywork: rumpled beige cardigan over a mustard shirt, crooked brown tie, messy thinning hair, round tortoiseshell glasses, a lanyard with a blank white badge, holding a tall wobbling stack of paper files against his chest and grinning mischievously at the camera. Standing in a dim, cluttered corporate office. Cinematic lighting, 35mm, shallow depth of field. No text, no letters, no logos.

The woman from the reference image, same face, hair and grey blazer, now sits in a bright open-plan sales office cubicle in daytime, a small white wireless earbud in each ear. She laughs warmly and says clearly in a confident American female voice: "Perfect. Tuesday at ten. See you then!" She taps her laptop once and instantly smiles at the next person: "Hi Mark, it's Maya." Energetic, upbeat, slight handheld camera.

The man from the reference image, same face, messy hair, rumpled white shirt and loose tie, slowly rises and peeks over a grey office cubicle wall, bewildered and exasperated, and says in a frustrated American male voice: "How have you talked to eleven people in sixty-six minutes? I can't get anyone on the phone!" Camera from the neighbouring cubicle looking up at him, comedic timing.

The woman from the reference image, same face, hair and grey blazer, sitting in a bright open-plan office cubicle in daytime, pulls one small white earbud out of her ear, swivels her chair toward someone standing above her and says with a friendly, amused grin in a confident American female voice: "You haven't heard of Connect and Sell? A week of prospecting in four hours." She pops the earbud back in and turns back to her laptop.

The grinning older man in the beige cardigan, mustard shirt, round glasses and lanyard from the first reference image perches casually on the edge of a cluttered office desk. At the desk sits the tired man in the rumpled white shirt and loose tie from the second reference image, on a desk phone. The cardigan man looks straight into the camera and says cheerfully in a smug, playful older American male voice: "I'm Busywork. I live in every sales team." Then he tips a huge stack of business cards onto the tired man's lap; cards scatter everywhere and the tired man groans. Comedic, punchy, slight push-in.

In a grey office cubicle, the grinning older man in the beige cardigan and round glasses from the first reference image slaps a thick printed phone list down onto the desk in front of the frustrated man in the white shirt and loose tie from the second reference image and says cheerfully: "Keep dialing, champ." The frustrated man stares at the pile in despair. Comedic timing, loud paper thud.
